e.etymology: A respelling of Josiah, from Hebrew Yoshiyahu, Yahweh supports. Josiah was the reforming king of Judah who came to the throne at the age of eight.
The Irish word for freedom, adopted as a given name in Ireland in the 20th century. Actress Saoirse Ronan carried it abroad after her 2007 breakthrough in Atonement.
namesakes: Saoirse Ronan (actress in Lady Bird and Little Women)

assoc.t: Saoirse Ronan, Irish actress

e.note: The Irish spelling trips up most Americans; expect to correct both spelling and pronunciation.

e.etymology: A modern coinage in the Ky- family with Kyrie, Kyler and Kylan; some hear it as a spelling of Kieran. Rams running back Kyren Williams has raised its profile.
namesakes: Kyren Williams (Los Angeles Rams running back)

e.meaning: uncertain; perhaps little rock or handsome
e.etymology: A spelling of Alan, a Breton name the Normans brought to Britain. Its meaning is uncertain; little rock and handsome are the usual guesses. The Allan spelling is favored in Scotland.
namesakes: Edgar Allan Poe (writer; Allan was his middle name)

e.etymology: From Welsh Gwenhwyfar, built on gwen, white or fair, with a second element usually read as smooth or as phantom. She is King Arthur's queen in legend, and Jennifer is the Cornish form of the same name.

assoc.t: Queen Guinevere, wife of King Arthur in legend

e.etymology: From the ancient city near the Jordan River whose walls fell to Joshua's trumpets in the Bible. The Hebrew name Yeriho is thought to be linked to the word for moon, or else to fragrance.

assoc.t: Jericho, ancient city whose walls fell in the Bible
Chris Jericho, pro wrestler

e.etymology: In Japan, Ren is most often written with the character for lotus and is a popular boys' name. In the US it also serves as a short form of names like Lauren and Renee and as a spelling of Wren.

assoc.t: Kylo Ren, villain of the Star Wars sequel trilogy
Ren, the chihuahua of The Ren & Stimpy Show
Ren McCormack, the hero of Footloose

e.etymology: The French feminine of Simon, from Hebrew Shim'on, he has heard. In Italy Simone is the men's form of the same name.
namesakes: Simone Biles (most decorated gymnast in history)
Simone de Beauvoir (French philosopher, author of The Second Sex)

assoc.t: Simone Biles, Olympic champion gymnast
Nina Simone, jazz and soul singer (her stage surname)

e.etymology: A Latin American Spanish form of the Arabic name Jamila, from jamil, beautiful. In the US it is used mostly by Latino families.

e.meaning: from Arcy, a place in France
e.etymology: A Norman surname, d'Arcy, for someone from Arcy in northern France. In Ireland it also anglicizes O Dorchaidhe, descendant of the dark one. Americans have used it mainly for girls since the mid-1900s.
namesakes: Fitzwilliam Darcy (hero of Jane Austen's Pride and Prejudice)
Darcy Lewis (Kat Dennings's character in the Thor films)

assoc.t: Mr. Darcy of Pride and Prejudice

e.etymology: From Latin lilia, the plural of lilium, lily; it also works as a Latin-style form of Lily. It is the form of Lily used in Spanish, Italian and the Slavic languages.

e.meaning: grace; a medieval pet form of Ann, also of Agnes
e.etymology: A medieval English pet form of Ann and of Annis, the everyday form of Agnes, in the same pattern as Betsy and Patsy. It became a name in its own right in the 1700s.
namesakes: Nancy Reagan (First Lady)
Nancy Pelosi (Speaker of the House)
Nancy Drew (teen detective of the mystery novels)

assoc.t: Nancy Drew, the teen detective
Negative Nancy, a phrase for a pessimist
Nancy, a city in northeastern France

e.note: Negative Nancy is a common phrase for a complainer, and nancy is a dated British slur for an effeminate man.

e.etymology: The Russian pet form of Natalya, from Latin natalis, of birth, in the sense of Christ's birthday. English speakers adopted it in the 20th century, helped by Natasha Rostova in Tolstoy's War and Peace.
namesakes: Natasha Romanoff (Marvel's Black Widow)
Natasha Lyonne (actress)
Natasha Bedingfield (pop singer)

assoc.t: Natasha Romanoff, Marvel's Black Widow
Natasha Rostova of War and Peace
Natasha, the spy in Rocky and Bullwinkle

e.etymology: Made known by the angel Castiel on the TV series Supernatural, who first appeared in 2008. The writers adapted the name from Cassiel, an angel of Jewish and Christian tradition.

assoc.t: the angel on the TV series Supernatural

e.etymology: From Old English Aelfraed, from aelf, elf, and raed, counsel. The fame of Alfred the Great, the 9th-century king of Wessex, kept it alive after the Norman Conquest, and it was revived in the 1700s.
namesakes: Alfred Hitchcock (film director)
Alfred the Great (9th-century English king)
Alfred Nobel (founder of the Nobel Prizes)

assoc.t: Alfred Pennyworth, Batman's butler

e.etymology: From Hebrew Neriyah, the Lord is my lamp. In the Old Testament Neriah is a man, the father of Jeremiah's scribe Baruch; American parents now give it mostly to girls.
A modern spelling of Avery, an English surname from the Norman French form of Alfred, Old English Aelfraed, elf counsel. The -i ending marks it as a girls' name.
A modern coinage that extends Kyle with the -en ending of Kellen and Jalen. Kyle is a Scottish name from Gaelic caol, a narrow strait.
In Serbian, Croatian and Bosnian it is read as da, to give, plus mir, peace. Among Tatars and Kazakhs the same name comes from Arabic damir, the inner self or conscience.
A short form of Elisabeth, from Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath. It became a name of its own in the 20th century and was the top US girls' name through most of the 1960s.
namesakes: Lisa Simpson (brainy daughter on The Simpsons)
Lisa Kudrow (actress, Phoebe on Friends)
Lisa Marie Presley (singer, daughter of Elvis)

assoc.t: Lisa Simpson of The Simpsons
Lisa, singer in the K-pop group Blackpink
the Mona Lisa, Leonardo da Vinci's portrait

e.etymology: A short form of Henrietta and other names ending in -etta, such as Antonietta. Henrietta is the feminine of Henry, from Germanic words for home and ruler. Etta stood on its own in the US by the 1880s.
namesakes: Etta James (blues and soul singer of At Last)

assoc.t: Etta James, singer of At Last

e.etymology: The Scandinavian form of Andrew, a medieval everyday form of Andreas, from Greek andreios, manly. It has been one of the most common men's names in Sweden for centuries.
namesakes: Anders Celsius (astronomer who devised the Celsius scale)

e.meaning: from Brodie in Scotland; perhaps muddy place or ditch
e.etymology: A Scottish surname from the lands of Brodie in Moray. The place name is of uncertain meaning, perhaps from Gaelic brothach, muddy place, or an old word for a ditch.

assoc.t: brodie, slang for a bro or close friend

e.etymology: A Spanish-language spelling of Sarai, the name Abraham's wife bore in Genesis before she was renamed Sarah. Sarai is traditionally read as my princess.
A modern American coinage, a spelling of Jamir that joins the Ja- opening of Jamal and Jamar to the sound of Amir.
A spelling of Malaya, which in Tagalog is the word for free. In American use it also follows the sound of names such as Maliyah and Amaya.
A respelling of Aiden, the English form of Irish Aodhan, a pet form of Aodh, fire. The E spelling spells out the long A sound.
The Latin word for light, the root of Lucia and Lucius and the name of the scientific unit of illumination. Its use as a given name is recent, for both boys and girls.
namesakes: Lux Lisbon (central sister in The Virgin Suicides)

assoc.t: lux, the unit of illumination; short for luxury
Lux, a champion in the game League of Legends

e.etymology: A modern American name on the pattern of Amari and Jamari with the popular Da- opening. It also resembles Damaris, a woman's name in the New Testament.

From Hebrew Elisheva, my God is an oath, by way of Greek Elisabet. This s spelling is the one in the King James New Testament and the standard form in German, French, Dutch and the Scandinavian languages.
namesakes: Elisabeth Moss (actress, The Handmaid's Tale and Mad Men)
Elisabeth Shue (actress, The Karate Kid and Leaving Las Vegas)
Elisabeth Hasselbeck (TV host)

e.etymology: An English surname that began as a nickname for a refined or courtly person, from Old French curteis, the source of the word courteous. It has been a first name since the 1800s.
namesakes: Curtis Mayfield (soul singer and songwriter)
Curtis Jackson (rapper known as 50 Cent)

e.etymology: The name of Lehi's wife in the Book of Mormon, published in 1830, and used mostly by Latter-day Saint families. It resembles Sarah and Mariah.

assoc.t: Sariah, wife of Lehi in the Book of Mormon
